title: Permissible-centre dilatation lowers the section defect
statement:
Let $R$ be a discrete valuation ring with uniformizer $\pi$, fraction field $K$ and residue field $k$ [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring], and choose a strict henselization $A=R^{\mathrm{sh}}$ [def-sc-ring-strict-henselization]. Let $X\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ be flat and locally of finite type with smooth generic fibre [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-flat-morphism, def-weil-finite-type-morphism, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. Let $Y\hookrightarrow X_k$ be a closed subscheme [def-weil-closed-immersion, def-pc-fibre-product]. Assume (N): on each affine open of $Y$, the intersection of the kernels of evaluation at the reductions of the points $a\in X(A)$ with $a_k\in Y$ is zero. Let $U\subseteq Y$ be open, smooth over $k$, and assume $\Omega^1_{X/R}|_U$ is locally free of finite rank [def-sc-relative-differential-sheaf, def-pc-module-pullback]; locally free means locally isomorphic to a finite direct sum of structure sheaves. Let $d:X'\to X$ be the dilatation, defined on $\operatorname{Spec}B\subset X$ by $\operatorname{Spec}B[I/\pi]$, where $I$ is the inverse image of the ideal of $Y$ in $B/\pi B$ and $B[I/\pi]\subset B[1/\pi]$ is generated by the elements $b/\pi$ with $b\in I$. For every $a:\operatorname{Spec}A\to X$ whose closed point lies in $U$, its unique lift $a':\operatorname{Spec}A\to X'$ satisfies
$$\delta_{X'}(a')\leq\max\{0,\delta_X(a)-1\}.$$
Here $\delta_X(a)=\operatorname{length}_A(\{v\in\Gamma(\operatorname{Spec}A,a^*\Omega^1_{X/R}):\exists\,0\ne t\in A,\ tv=0\})$ [def-weil-pbc-module-length], and similarly for $X'$. No group structure or quasi-compactness of $X$ or $Y$ is assumed.

source.place: BLR 3.3 Proposition 5 and proof, printed pp.68-71 (PDF pages 74-77), with condition (N) defined on p.67; local finite type refinement using the proof's first sentence (locality on X). Local PDF WANTED; primary-source scan read at https://www.math.stonybrook.edu/~kamenova/homepage_files/Bosch_Raynaud_Neron_Model_tc.pdf.

proof.text: Let $K$ be the separable closure used for $A$, $\Omega$ an algebraic closure of $K$ and $\bar x:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ the geometric point over the closed point [def-weil-geometric-point]. An $R$-map from an etale $R$-algebra $S$ to $\Omega$ factors through the residue field of a prime of $S$ over $\pi R$, which is finite separable over $k$, hence lands in $K$; so the pairs $(S,\chi:S\to K)$ of [def-sc-ring-strict-henselization] and the affine pointed etale neighbourhoods of $\bar x$ are the same index category with the same diagram, and $A\cong\mathcal O^{\mathrm{sh}}_{\operatorname{Spec}R,\bar x}$ as $R$-algebras [def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-limit]. Hence [lem-sc-strict-henselization-dvr], applied to $Y=\operatorname{Spec}R$ whose local ring $R$ is Noetherian, makes $A$ a DVR, and by [lem-sc-ring-strict-henselization-local-maximal-ideal] its maximal ideal is $\pi A$. Every section in question lies in any open neighbourhood of its closed image, since an open subset of the spectrum of a local ring containing the closed point is the whole spectrum. Apply [lem-sfb-adapted-smooth-ambient] at that image and write $X=\operatorname{Spec}D\hookrightarrow\operatorname{Spec}C$, $W=Y\cap X\subseteq U$, $D=C/H$, $J=(\pi,z_1,\ldots,z_n)$. This replacement preserves (N): the sections reducing into an affine open of $Y$ already factor through the chosen open of $X$. Use $N=r+n$ and the supplied differential basis. Differential pullback and [lem-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials-localization] identify the original section modules with the modules on this chart.

source.place: 3.3 Proposition 5 proof, locality and adapted ambient construction, pp.68-69; Stacks 0AP3 and 04GP for the strict henselization.

proof.text: We prove $H\subseteq J^2$, retaining the essential use of (N). For $f\in H$, write $f=\pi g+\sum_jz_jg_j$. The differential of $f$ maps to zero in $\Omega_{D/R}\otimes_D C/J$. The isomorphism in the ambient-coordinate node therefore gives $0=\sum_j\overline{g_j}\,dz_j$ in $\Omega_{C/R}\otimes_C C/J$. Its basis gives $g_j\in J$. Thus $f=\pi g+h$ with $h\in J^2$. For every section $b$ reducing into $W$, all elements of $J$ evaluate into $\pi A$, so $h(b)\in\pi^2A$ and $0=f(b)=\pi g(b)+h(b)$ imply $g(b)\in\pi A$. Condition (N) on $W$ forces $g\bmod J=0$. Hence $f\in J^2$. This works for every $f$, without choosing generators yet.

source.place: 3.3 Proposition 5 proof, key claim on p.69 (H and J denote the source I and J).

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-smooth-centre-dilatation-coordinates] to obtain $C'=C[J/\pi]$ and $z'_j=z_j/\pi$. The section map $C\to A$ sends each $z_j$ into $\pi A$, so it extends uniquely by $z'_j\mapsto a(z_j)/\pi$. Its kernel contains $HC'$ and, since $A$ has no $\pi$-torsion, contains the saturation $H'=\{c\in C':\pi^m c\in HC'\text{ for some }m\geq0\}$. The image of $C'$ in $D[1/\pi]$ is exactly $D[(J/H)/\pi]$, and its kernel is exactly $H'$, by clearing a power of $\pi$. Thus $D'=C'/H'$ is the dilatation algebra in the statement and the extended map gives its unique lifted section $a'$.

source.place: 3.2 affine construction; 3.3 Proposition 5 proof, p.70, saturated defining ideal.

proof.text: For $f\in H\subseteq J^2$, the element $f^\sharp=f/\pi^2$ belongs to $C'$, since $J^2C'\subseteq\pi^2C'$. It lies in $H'$. Write $df=\sum_i b_i\,dy_i+\sum_jc_j\,dz_j$ and $df^\sharp=\sum_i b_i^\sharp\,dy_i+\sum_jc_j^\sharp\,dz'_j$. Differentiate $f=\pi^2f^\sharp$ in $C'$ and compare the basis coefficients using $dz_j=\pi dz'_j$. Since $C'$ is $R$-flat, cancellation gives $b_i=\pi^2b_i^\sharp$ and $c_j=\pi c_j^\sharp$. After evaluation along the lifted section, each row for $f^\sharp$ is therefore the row for $f$ with the $y$ columns divided by $\pi^2$ and the $z$ columns divided by $\pi$.

source.place: 3.3 Proposition 5 proof, differential coefficient equations on p.70.

proof.text: Choose finite ideal generators $f_1,\ldots,f_s$ of $H$ and $h_1,\ldots,h_t$ of $H'$; these exist because $C,C'$ are Noetherian in the two coordinate nodes. By [lem-weil-pbc-jacobi-zariski-differential-maps], quotient differentials are presented by the rows $df_\lambda$ and $dh_\mu$. After tensoring along the section, these remain presentations: explicitly tensoring a quotient $E/L$ gives the quotient of the tensor of $E$ by the image of $L$, as follows directly from the tensor-product universal property. Thus $V_a=A^N/L$ and $V_{a'}=A^N/L'$, with relation rows evaluated in the respective supplied bases. Any $dh$ with $h\in H'$ gives a row in $L'$, since differentiating $h=\sum u_\mu h_\mu$ and evaluating kills the terms $h_\mu\,du_\mu$.

source.place: 3.3 Lemma 2 presentation argument, p.66; Proposition 5 proof, p.70; Stacks 00RU for quotient differentials.

proof.text: Let $F=\operatorname{Frac}A$. The row spans of $L$ and $L'$ over $F$ have the same dimension $q$: after inverting $\pi$, $C'[1/\pi]=C[1/\pi]$ and $H'[1/\pi]=H[1/\pi]$, while the differential bases differ by the invertible diagonal matrix with entries $1$ on $dy_i$ and $\pi$ on $dz'_j$. More explicitly an element of either localized ideal is a sum of multiples of the other's generators; differentiating and evaluating at the section kills the generator times coefficient-differential terms. Consequently their relation spans are identified by this diagonal basis change. This proves rank equality without a dimension or equidimensionality assertion about the generic fibre.

source.place: 3.3 Proposition 5 proof, Jacobian ranks on pp.70-71; explicit localization argument.

proof.text:
If $q>0$, [lem-sfb-dvr-relation-minors-length] gives a $q$-minor $\Delta$ of the evaluated rows $df_\lambda$ with $v(\Delta)=\delta_X(a)$. Use the same rows and columns for $df_\lambda^\sharp$; these are relations in $L'$ by step 5. If $p$ selected columns are $y$ columns, step 4 gives $\Delta^\sharp=\pi^{-(q+p)}\Delta$. Include these extra relation rows together with the rows $dh_\mu$ in a generating matrix for $L'$; they do not change its quotient or rank. Applying the same minors formula to that matrix gives
$$\delta_{X'}(a')\leq v(\Delta^\sharp)=\delta_X(a)-q-p\leq\delta_X(a)-1.$$
All evaluated entries of this minor lie in $A$, so its valuation is nonnegative; the inequality in particular forces $\delta_X(a)\geq1$. If $q=0$, both relation spans have rank zero and hence both submodules are zero, since $A^N\hookrightarrow F^N$ is injective. Both section modules are free and both defects are zero. These two cases give the stated maximum, including the zero-defect and empty-coordinate cases.

source.place: 3.3 Proposition 5 proof, minors comparison and zero-codimension case, pp.70-71; the zero-rank case is handled directly in the relation modules.
